Document Analysis Activity
Unit 1 · Colonial Foundations
Establishing
the Colonies

Historians don't just read about the past — they analyze sources left behind by people who lived it. In this activity, you will examine primary sources from the early colonial period to understand how different groups experienced the founding of European colonies in North America.

✍️
Synthesis & Analysis — After completing your assigned documents, you will write three short responses: analyzing point of view and bias, constructing a historical argument, and identifying missing perspectives. (~10–12 min)
Total estimated time: — minutes · Export your completed work as a PDF to submit.
Documents Complete
Great work. Now bring it all together in the synthesis below.

Historians do more than summarize sources — they evaluate them critically and use them to build arguments. Use the documents you analyzed to complete each section below.

Part 1 — Point of View & Bias
Choose two documents from this activity. For each one, explain how the author's point of view, purpose, or situation may have shaped what they included — or left out.
A.Choose a document and identify its author (or creator). Explain how their background or purpose may have influenced what they chose to show or say.
0 characters
B.Choose a second document. What might this source be leaving out? Whose voice or experience is missing from it?
0 characters
Part 2 — Historical Argument
Write a paragraph responding to the question below. Your paragraph must include a clear claim and use specific evidence from at least two documents to support it.
Writing prompt: Using at least two documents from this activity, explain how European colonization affected different groups of people living in North America during the 1600s and 1700s.
0 characters
Part 3 — Missing Perspectives
No document set tells the complete story. Think about who or what is not represented in the sources you analyzed.
A.Identify one group of people whose perspective is missing from these documents entirely. Who are they?
0 characters
B.What would their account likely add to our understanding of the early colonial period? What might they say that none of these documents say?
